cultural_notes: Findlay Market (1855) in Over-the-Rhine is Cincinnati's historic public market — a brick hall with outdoor farm sheds, a civic food anchor for the Ohio River city (source: findlaymarket.org)

The Lebanon orchard belt (Warren County, ~30 mi NE of Cincinnati) is the featured frontier — Irons Fruit Farm (Lebanon) and Hidden Valley Orchards supply pawpaws (Sep), apples (Oct), pumpkins (Oct-Nov) and cider (source: Irons Fruit Farm; Hidden Valley Orchards)

Pawpaws (Asimina triloba) are Ohio's native custard fruit, peak mid-September in Ohio River bottomlands — tropical banana-mango flavor, short season, foraged + orchard grown (source: Ohio State Extension pawpaw notes; USDA)
Kroger (Cincinnati-founded, HQ) is the dominant grocer; Meijer is the Midwest supercenter; Findlay Market is the public-market anchor (source: Kroger footprint)
